newsitem.title: UK: World Bank to borrow up to $5.5 bln by end June.
newsitem.headline: World Bank to borrow up to $5.5 bln by end June.

text.p: The World Bank could borrow up to $5.5 billion on the international capital markets between now and the end of its fiscal year in June, an official told Reuters on Wednesday.

"Our fiscal year runs from July 1996 to June 1997 and we want to raise $13 billion to $14 billion equivalent on the international capital markets," Gumersindo Oliveros, senior manager of capital markets operations at the World Bank said.
"So far $8.5 billion equivalent has been raised. If we continue to have good market opportunities, like we have had so far, we will go up to $14 billion," he said.
He was referring to medium- and long-term borrowing.
In the 1996 calender year, the World Bank raised $13 billion and Oliveros said this amount could be matched in 1997.
"If we look at calender 1997 it's reasonable to assume that we will be doing a similar level of funding as in 1996," Oliveros, in London for a bond conference, said.
"Beyond that our borrowing programme will depend of the level of disbursements we have on our loan portfolio and also the redemptions that are falling due," he said.
Earlier, Oliveros said the World Bank was considering a euro Eurobond and would launch such a deal as soon as it became cost-effective to do so.
